text.p: TORONTO, July 24 Reuter) - The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE GLOBE AND MAIL: No reprieve for hospitals: Women's College supporters say changes to plan won't guarantee equity in care
Body thought to be Cunanan's: SWAT teams storm houseboat
Britain probes bank deposits: Search begins for amount of money it seized from victims of Nazi Germany
Canadians pore over Swiss bank-account list
Salmon talks set to start again: Axworthy agrees to U.S. demand
Oder at highest level of century: German troops sent in as dike breaks
Report on Business Section: Business plans spending spree: Earmarks $83.8-billion for infrastructure, up 14 percent from '96; governments also open purses
Bre-X shop had beer, cigarettes-and gold: Whoever was behind the salting scam didn't have far to go. A Dayak man was known to sell panned gold at the Busang general store.
BCE's 29 percent profit rise not enough for CEO: Calls Bell's contrubution 'unsatisfactory'
Boeing merger gets green light: Firm grants 11th-hour concession to EC

THE FINANCIAL POST: Capital spending roars back: Expenditures on new plant and equipment will hit a record this year, StatsCan says, rising 11 percent to $110.9B. That's the biggest hike since 1993 and is helping drive the economy ahead
Bre-X scam unlikely one-man job, experts say
